steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on SAMAug, a method that automatically adds extra point/box prompts to the Segment Anything Model to improve its segmentation. Give the background on SAM and foundation models, the ambiguity problem with simple prompts, what SAMAug does and how we evaluate it, and our contributions.

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Recent progress in large pre-trained models has inspired a series of developments of foundational models in computer vision. Among them, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) stands out as a new interactive model that is designed specifically for image segmentation tasks and the downstream applications that follow.

SAM represents the paradigm shift in artificial intelligence toward large-scale, general-purposed "foundation" models. The SAM model shows that it is feasible to do multi-task image segmentation with a zero-shot learning approach. It also lets the user give "prompts" in the form of points, bounding boxes, or dense masks to do the segmentation with an in-context-learning scheme. But simple prompts like a single point lead to ambiguities in the SAM model, which is also discussed in the original SAM paper. The multi-mask prediction and the confidence score-based result selection scheme used by SAM can solve some of the ambiguities, but we observed that it is also possible to generate more point prompts automatically to improve the performance of SAM.

- SAMAug
  - novel visual point augmentation method, extra segmentation masks using SAM

  - four point sampling approaches: random, maximum difference entropy, maximum distance, saliency-based
  - inner- and outer-bounding box augmentation for box prompts
- Experiments
  - COCO, Fundus, COVIDQU-Ex, ISIC2018

  - more possibilities for human inputs in visual prompts
  - step toward prompt-based augmentation for CV: fewer user inputs, better performance

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Recent progress in large pre-trained models has inspired a series of developments of foundational models in computer vision. Among them, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) stands out as a new interactive model that is designed specifically for image segmentation tasks and the downstream applications that follow.

SAM represents the paradigm shift in artificial intelligence toward large-scale, general-purposed "foundation" models. The SAM model shows that it is feasible to do multi-task image segmentation with a zero-shot learning approach. It also lets the user give "prompts" in the form of points, bounding boxes, or dense masks to do the segmentation with an in-context-learning scheme. But simple prompts like a single point lead to ambiguities in the SAM model, which is also discussed in the original SAM paper. The multi-mask prediction and the confidence score-based result selection scheme used by SAM can solve some of the ambiguities, but we observed that it is also possible to generate more point prompts automatically to improve the performance of SAM.

In this work, we propose SAMAug, a new visual point augmentation method that generates additional segmentation masks using SAM. SAMAug does prompt (point or bounding-box) augmentation based on the initial segmentation results that SAM gives with a single point or box prompt, and then puts them into the prompt-based segmentation by SAM. We evaluate four sampling approaches for point prompts: random, maximum difference entropy, maximum distance, and saliency-based. We also investigated inner- and outer-bounding box augmentation for box prompts.

We run experiments on the COCO, Fundus, COVIDQU-Ex, and ISIC2018 datasets and show that SAMAug can improve the performance of SAM, especially with the maximum distance and saliency model point selection approaches. The results show more possibilities for incorporating human inputs in a visual prompt setting. SAMAug is an important step toward prompt-based augmentation methods for computer vision that can reduce user inputs and improve model performance.

The key contributions of this study are:

- We develop SAMAug, a new visual point augmentation framework that generates additional prompts for SAM without extra manual operations.

- We propose a visual prompt augmentation theory that is based on the invariance in prompt selection.

- We tested different visual prompt augmentation techniques with experiments on one general-domain dataset and three medical-domain datasets, and found which augmentation techniques are the most effective (maximum distance and saliency).

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Recent advances in large pre-trained models [1,2] have inspired a series of developments of foundational models in computer vision [3,4]. Among these, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) [5] stands out as a novel interactive model designed specifically for image segmentation tasks and subsequent downstream applications.

SAM represents the paradigm shift in artificial intelligence towards large-scale, general-purposed "foundation" models [6,7]. The SAM model demonstrates the feasibility of performing multi-task image segmentation in a zero-shot learning approach. It also allows "prompts" in the form of user-provided points, bounding boxes, or dense masks to be used to perform the segmentation via an in-context-learning scheme. However, simple prompts such as a single point lead to ambiguities in the SAM model, as also discussed in the original paper of SAM [5]. While the multi-mask prediction and confidence score-based result selection scheme adopted by SAM can resolve some of these ambiguities, we observed that additional point prompts can also be generated automatically to improve the performance of SAM. In this work, we propose SAMAug, a novel visual point augmentation method for generating additional segmentation masks using SAM. SAMAug performs prompt (point or bounding-box) augmentation based on the initial segmentation results from SAM using a single point or box prompt, and then incorporates them into the prompt-based segmentation by SAM. We evaluate four sampling approaches for point prompts: random, maximum difference entropy, maximum distance, and saliency-based. We also investigated inner- and outer-bounding box augmentation for box prompts.

With experiments on the COCO, Fundus, COVIDQU-Ex, and ISIC2018 datasets, we show that SAMAug can improve SAM's performance, especially when the maximum distance and saliency model point selection approaches are used. Our results show more possibilities for incorporating human inputs in a visual prompt setting. SAMAug is an important step towards prompt-based augmentation methods for computer vision that can reduce user inputs and improve model performance.

This study makes the following key contributions:

- We develop a novel visual point augmentation framework, SAMAug, which generates additional prompts for SAM without extra manual operations.

- We propose a visual prompt augmentation theory based on the invariance in prompt selection.

- We tested different visual prompt augmentation techniques with experiments on one general-domain and three medical-domain datasets and identified the most effective ones (maximum distance and saliency).
